verdicts.rationale: The related-work discussion explicitly describes heuristic or text-based expert selection and missing quantitative invocation criteria.
Section 3.1 specifies concrete visual queries, CLIP-based grounding, and averaging of query-specific spatial maps.
Equations 3–5 combine relevant-region semantic deviation and irrelevant-region stability, weighted using entropy and contrast.
Section 3.3 explicitly describes rendering these structured outputs onto images and re-querying through the existing vision encoder.
The method reuses original masks, selects the greatest positive utilization gain, and skips refinement when none improves the baseline.
The models, experts, mask count, and Top-k/Bottom-k settings are correct, but the claim omits adaptive adjustment of masking ratios in Hybrid mode, which the comprehensive experiments use.
Table 1 identifies 16 benchmarks, and Section 4.1 specifies the five categories, subsets, GRAY rendering, and Hybrid masking.
Section 4.2 names all four datasets, highlight rendering, the evaluator, and the four response categories.
Both numerical changes and their directions match the IDEFICS row in Table 1.
The captioning discussion explicitly reports the Flickr decrease from 57.3 to 55.9.
The Qwen2.5-VL COCO Caption hallucination entry reports 48.24/26.13, with values defined as category percentages.
Table 3 identifies PaliGemma and reports all three stated comparisons, including the 70.39% average cost reduction.
The introduction and discussion explicitly acknowledge tuning requirements, utilization variability, and heuristic masking sensitivity.
The paper explicitly characterizes DnR as reinforcing access to existing knowledge and unable to recover unknown facts.
The cited passages establish the utilization criterion, rendering integration without retraining, and an approximate learned replacement for exhaustive selection.
